chunks: He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad al-Zayyat reported to me, who said: Ali ibn Mahrawayh al-Qazwini narrated to us, who said: Dawood ibn Sulaiman al-Ghazi narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Ridha Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them both) saying:
"Whoever has acquired a brother for the sake of God has indeed acquired a house in Paradise."

He said: And Abul Hasan al-Rahbi the grammarian recited to me the following verses by al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Tamimi: "Indeed a man who has lived fifty years is truly near to the watering-place of his return. When you pass a day alone in your life, do not say 'I am alone,' but rather say 'Over me is an observer.' When the generation in which you lived has passed, and you are left behind in a new generation, then you are a stranger."
And all praise be to God, and His blessings upon our master Muhammad the Prophet and his pure and purified family.

key_terms.استفاد أخا في الله: Acquired a brother for the sake of God -- forming a sincere bond of brotherhood motivated purely by faith
key_terms.بيتا في الجنة: A house in Paradise -- the spiritual reward for sincere brotherhood
key_terms.رقيب: Observer/Watcher -- referring to God's constant surveillance over human actions
key_terms.غريب: Stranger -- one who outlives their generation and feels alienated in the next

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for brotherhood for the sake of God according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Ridha (AS), the eighth Shia Imam, recorded in al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Mufid, teaches the immense spiritual reward of forming brotherhood for the sake of God -- equating it to earning a house in Paradise. The teaching was delivered in the context of 3rd/4th century AH scholarly gatherings where brotherhood (ukhuwwa) was considered a pillar of communal solidarity. The session concludes with poetry by al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Tamimi reminding listeners of the brevity of life, God's constant watchfulness, and the loneliness of outliving one's peers.
